_README: SEMANTIC drift between liquidretail_backend and liquidretail_adgen — the class of
divergence that no hash can see.
verifyVendorDrift.js answers 'did the bytes we last looked at change?'. That question
is blind to two real failure modes:
1. A fix lands in ONE repo. The other copy's backend hash never moved, so drift never
fires; the manifest records a 'fork'/'unported' reason and the obligation goes quiet.
2. The SAME bug exists in N copies, byte-identical. There is no drift at all — both
sides agree, and both are wrong. Byte-equality actively certifies the bug.
This file is the declarative answer: named invariants, each a pattern that must not
appear (or must appear) in a named set of files, checked across BOTH repos by
scripts/verifySharedInvariants.js. A fix is then provably a fix everywhere, not just
in the copy someone happened to open.
`acknowledged` is NOT A MUTE BUTTON. It follows scripts/expected-failures.json's
contract exactly: an acknowledged instance that is GONE fails the run as a STALE entry.
You cannot fix an instance and leave it listed, and you cannot park a finding here and
forget it — removing the entry is part of the fix, in the same commit. Every entry needs
a reason someone can act on and a removeWhen. 'known issue' is not a reason.
A NEW match that is not acknowledged FAILS. That is the whole point.
`count` (optional, default 1) is how many instances an entry attests to in that file.
Entries are keyed on repo+path, NOT on a line number — a line-keyed entry goes stale on
every unrelated edit above it, which trains people to bulk-update this file without
reading it. But repo+path alone would let an acknowledged file HIDE a new instance:
acknowledge the hit at :68, and a second one added at :200 keys to the same entry and
passes silently. So the count is checked in BOTH directions — more than attested means a
new instance appeared beside a known one; fewer means some were fixed and the entry now
overstates the debt. Both fail.

rationale: A catalog title must never be interpolated into a labelled `Product:` field of a
prompt sent to a generative IMAGE or VIDEO model.
INCIDENT (2026-08-26, visually proven on a delivered Pelagic Gear master): the line
`Product: Vaportek.` was read by Atlas Omni as a brand-name render instruction. It
fabricated a complete 'VAPORTEK' chest lockup and a fake neck tag over the real
small PELAGIC fish-mark. Vision-QC correctly terminal-rejected the $0.90 master,
with no regeneration. The existing `noText` directive already forbids generating new
logos and was NOT enough once a brand-sounding catalog title was also sitting in a
The fix was applied to adgen/src/services/veoPromptBuilder.js only. The identical
construct survived in three other copies across the two repos — which is exactly the
'one bug, three files, two repos, one fix' pattern this invariant exists to close.
PRODUCT FIDELITY plus the supplied reference images already identify the SKU, so this
line was optional context and is not load-bearing for any parser.

Matches the pattern but is a DIFFERENT hazard class and deliberately excluded, not overlooked. Its `Product: ${productName}` subject line goes to gemini-2.5-flash to structure a review narrative into JSON (a text LLM extracting text). Nothing renders it. The Vaportek failure was an image/video model painting the title onto the product as artwork; a text extractor cannot do that.

patternNote: Requires a template-literal interpolation (backtick, then `Product:`, then `${`).
That is what discriminates live code from the comments documenting the fix:
contains `Product: {title}` — neither has `${`, so neither matches. This is
deliberately a narrow structural pattern rather than a comment-stripping lexer:
hand-rolled JS comment stripping desyncs on regex literals and would be a worse
bug than the one it is checking for.

acknowledged.reason: DORMANT, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON IT LOOKS LIKE — and one env var from live. Same catalog-title interpolation the Vaportek incident proved harmful, in the GPT-storyboard path. It is NOT gated by VEO_USE_GPT_STORYBOARD: config/defaults.env:395 ships that flag `true` in BOTH repos and no render.yaml, Dockerfile, src/config.js, or SystemConfig overrides it, so enabled() returns true. What actually makes it unreachable is the provider router: videoRouter.activeProvider() defaults to 'atlas' (videoRouter.js:29, VIDEO_PROVIDER=atlas committed at defaults.env:394), and on the atlas path prepareStoryboard returns {storyboard:null} ('Storyboard retired on the Atlas path', atlasVideoService.js:4344). generateStoryboard has exactly ONE production caller, aiVideoReferenceService.js:320, reached only from videoRouter's non-atlas else branch. Set VIDEO_PROVIDER=vertex and this line composes a paid Vertex Veo prompt. The module's own header comment ('Off by default', veoStoryboardService.js:10) describes a gate that is not the real one. Acknowledged rather than fixed here because this PR is documentation + enforcement scope: editing a generative video prompt is a behavioural money-path change needing its own PR and owner sign-off, and bundling it silently would hide it.
acknowledged.removeWhen: the `Product: ${title}` interpolation is removed from adgen/src/services/veoStoryboardService.js, matching the veoPromptBuilder fix — then delete this entry in the same commit

acknowledged.reason: The backend twin of the entry above — byte-identical to adgen's copy, which is why the vendor manifest correctly calls it 'synced' and why no hash check can ever flag it. Both copies agree and both are wrong.
acknowledged.removeWhen: the same removal lands in liquidretail_backend/services/veoStoryboardService.js — then delete this entry

acknowledged.reason: THE UNPORTED FIX. adgen fixed this exact line on 2026-08-26; the backend copy is still the pre-fix blob. The vendor manifest records the obligation in prose ('a human must apply the same edit in liquidretail_backend'), which nothing enforced. This entry plus the manifest's new `unported` status are what now make that obligation fail loudly instead of aging quietly.
